🔴 **The legal correction that will otherwise be made for you in the room.** **EN 301 549 V4.1.1 was published `2026-09-02`** and maps onto the European Accessibility Act's essential requirements — **but the EAA does not mandate sign language in education.** Its sign-language expectations attach to audiovisual media services and video-capable ICT devices. The driver for a signed track in European education is **national disability law plus UNCRPD Article 24**, and the market is **~1 million deaf sign-language users in the EU/EEA** (European Union of the Deaf), which also has an EAA-shortcomings report in progress (`T476`).

🔵 **Regulatory context already held and re-controlled this pass:** EU AI Act Annex III education high-risk duties apply from **`2027-12-02`** (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744); Article 50 transparency from `2026-08-02`; the **emotion-recognition prohibition in education has been in force since `2025-02-02`** — which matters here, because a camera pointed at a signing learner is a camera, and the boundary between pose estimation and affect inference has to be documented in the design, not argued after deployment.

🟢 **Adoption numbers read this pass:** Futuresource — **`67%` of teachers now use AI tools**, moving from pilots to structured implementation; Epson (`~3,360` respondents across UK/FR/IT/DE/ES/PL, July–August 2026) — **`80%` of teachers worry AI is arriving faster than schools can manage.** 🟢 **The second number is the sales frame for this register: a signed-track project is a *governed*, standards-anchored deliverable, which is what an anxious European institution will actually buy.**

🟢 **The engagement:** a university or national broadcaster-adjacent education body commissions a **signed glossary plus signed course content** in one national sign language — `signwriting-translation` + `sutton-signwriting/core` for the reviewable notation layer, the MIT chain for production, `MMS-Player` deployed as an isolated client-operated process to keep GPL-3.0 out of the deliverable. Recipes `P265`, `P267`.

#### 🆕 `p752` (`2026-11-10`) — 🟢 the ESCO procurement gate is now a dated regulation, and the open-source supply for its wallet layer is `0`

🟢 **This page's existing EMEA placement of the skills register is reaffirmed and sharpened — the demand signal has hardened from a buying theme into an instrument with a date.**

🔴 **The instrument:** the **EU Talent Pool Regulation took effect `2026-06-01`**, and it gives **ESCO the central role as the shared vocabulary** for matching skills and occupations across member states. The Commission's `2026-07` ESCO newsletter describes expanding use in **EURES** and **Europass** matching and introduces the Europass **"Smart CV"**, alongside an ongoing revamp of the ESCO skills pillar. 🔵 An implementer example the Commission itself publishes: **CPASS**, an AI-based skills-verification platform operating in **Kenya**, which maps each skill to an ESCO identifier and cites ESCO's skill-to-occupation links as the deciding factor — while noting that **ESCO's update cycle lags fast-moving sectors**, which is a real integration caveat rather than a detail.

🔴 **The measured supply against that live instrument is nil where it matters most:** `credential wallet europass` → **`0`** repositories, `labour market intelligence open source` → **`0`** (`T461`). 🟢 **This is the cleanest demand-without-supply signal in the register.**

🟢 **What EMEA does have, and it is the opposite asymmetry to North America — extraction is nearly free, platforms are absent:**

| Component | Repo | Grant — byte-read | Stars |
|---|---|---|---|
| Job-advert → skills extractor | [`nestauk/ojd_daps_skills`](https://github.com/nestauk/ojd_daps_skills) | 🟢 **MIT** | 🟢 **`162★`** |
| ESCO/ISCO text extractor | [`KonstantinosPetrakis/esco-skill-extractor`](https://github.com/KonstantinosPetrakis/esco-skill-extractor) | 🟢 **MIT** | `32★` |
| ESCO taxonomy extension | [`dkavargy/ESCOPlus`](https://github.com/dkavargy/ESCOPlus) | 🟢 **MIT** | `6★` |
| Full EU-funded pipeline | [`skillab-project`](https://github.com/skillab-project) (Horizon) | 🟡 **`EPL-2.0`**, `13 / 13` repos | `0★`–`1★` |

🔴 **`EPL-2.0` is the licence most often mis-summarised in this subject area and it needs a legal review, not a dependency bump:** file-scoped copyleft, a patent-retaliation clause, and **a commercial distributor must indemnify the other contributors** for liability arising from that commercial offering. 🟢 **If the review fails, substitute the MIT extractor** — it is the same dependency Skillab itself imports (`T460`), so results stay comparable.

🔵 **Opportunity, placed.** 🟢 **`P261` on [`../compose/patterns.md`](../compose/patterns.md) — curriculum-to-labour-market gap analysis — is the buyable engagement**, and ESCO is a **procurement gate**: an agent that speaks ESCO can be mapped to a European funding instrument and a national qualifications framework; one that invents its own taxonomy cannot be. 🔴 **The build is the authoring and registry surface**, because EMEA has no open-source equivalent of OSMT or the Credential Registry.

🔴 **Boundaries, stated.** **ESCO's own licence terms are not asserted anywhere in this pass** — `esco.ec.europa.eu` fails DNS resolution here, so counsel must read the Commission's terms from the Commission's page before ESCO content enters a deliverable. 🔴 **The Nordic national stack is outside this instrument entirely:** `user:JobtechSwe` — the Swedish Public Employment Service, publisher of the national occupational taxonomy and job-matching APIs a Nordic engagement would build against — exposes **`2` public GitHub repositories** (`ontology-files`, `2★`, no grant, last pushed `2019-12-06`; `anonymisering`, MIT, `2023-06-28`). The live taxonomy is on `jobtechdev.se`, also unreachable. 🔵 **`0` mentions across `752` passes was never negligence; it is the shape of a GitHub-only instrument** (`T396`, `T463`).

🔵 **Regulatory context.** The **AI Act** treats education AI affecting access, assessment or admissions as **high-risk**, **and recruitment systems likewise** — which puts a skills-matching agent in scope on *both* counts. Under the **Digital Omnibus** (political agreement `2026-05-07`, adopted June 2026, in force **`2026-07-27`**), stand-alone **Annex III obligations were deferred from `2026-08-02` to `2026-12-02`… specifically to `2 December 2027`**, with AI embedded in regulated products following **`2 August 2028`**. 🔴 **Read that as scoping runway, not a reprieve: a system designed now will be in scope when it ships.** An EU Council text of `2026-04-24` insists AI tools **support rather than replace or isolate teachers**, and a Commission brief of `2026-10-23` reports **only about a third of national school curricula include AI competences**. **UK:** DfE published **generative-AI product safety standards for education in January 2026**, and **Ofqual** issued coursework-integrity resources in **March 2026**. **Gulf:** Dubai's **KHDA** has issued explicit responsible-AI guidance to private schools.


#### 🆕 `p751` — the scheduling and assignment register, placed in EMEA

🔴 **This register sits directly on top of Annex III point 3 of the EU AI Act.** Point 3 covers four education functions, and **the first is admission or assignment of natural persons to educational institutions** — which is what a school-placement mechanism or an allocating timetabler does. The other three are evaluating learning outcomes, assessing the level of education a person will attain, and **monitoring prohibited behaviour during tests**.

⚠️ **This base does not state the date with confidence, and a proposal must not either.** Most sources read this pass place the Annex III high-risk obligations at **`2027-12-02`**, moved from `2026-08-02` by the **Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744** (Official Journal, `2026-07-24`). **At least one source argues point 3 was not amended by that regulation and therefore keeps its original date.** 🔵 **Verify against the Official Journal text before any client-facing deadline.** Nearer-term and less disputed: **chatbot transparency and AI-literacy obligations from August 2026**, and **emotion recognition has been prohibited in education since `2025-02-02`** with no grace period (`p750`'s finding, which still governs).

🔴 **The architectural lever, and it is the most commercially useful thing in this pass (`T449`).** The Act regulates *AI systems*. A hand-written CP-SAT or MIP model is a set of rules defined entirely by natural persons — the category the definition is generally read to exclude. **So the same business function may fall inside or outside Annex III depending on how it is built**: a deferred-acceptance mechanism or an explicit constraint model is plausibly out of scope; an LLM that *infers* the constraints, or a learned ranker that orders applicants, is plausibly in. 🟢 **Sell the classical solver as the compliance-cheap architecture and keep the LLM on the authoring side, where a human approves every constraint before it binds.** ⚠️ **This is an open legal reading, not settled law — it must be confirmed by counsel, and it cuts both ways: reaching for an LLM to prototype faster can convert an unregulated scheduler into a high-risk system.**

🟢 **EMEA has the best open supply in this register, and nobody placed it there deliberately (`T444`).** Permissive, maintained MCP adapters exist for **`4` national school portals, all EU/EEA**: EduPage (🇸🇰 **MIT**), Pronote (🇫🇷 **MIT**), WebUntis (🇦🇹🇩🇪 **MIT**) and Bakaláři (🇨🇿 — 🔴 **no grant, not usable**). The supply exists where the portal has a national install base. 🟢 **Consequence: a parent- or pupil-facing scheduling assistant in France, DACH or CEE starts from a licence review, not a reverse-engineering project.**

🔴 **The EMEA-specific instrument gap.** **FET**, widely deployed in European schools, is **unreachable from this environment** — `lalescu.ro` and `lalescu.ro/liviu/fet/` both return `000`, and the canonical GitHub addresses `404` (`T445`). An EMEA engagement that must evaluate FET needs a channel this pipeline does not have. Also EMEA-placed: [`chocoteam/choco-solver`](https://github.com/chocoteam/choco-solver) (**BSD-3-Clause**, IMT Atlantique 🇫🇷) and [`indico/indico`](https://github.com/indico/indico) (**MIT**, CERN 🇨🇭), both verified alive and pushed this pass.

#### 🆕 `p750` (2026-11-10) — the wellbeing and safeguarding layer: required to monitor, forbidden to infer affect, and both halves are dated

🔴 **This is the pincer, and it is the finding of the pass for this region.** The same school is under a
positive duty to monitor and a prohibition on inferring emotion, and a vendor that confuses the two
breaks the law rather than the contract.

**The duty — UK, and it is inspected.** **Keeping Children Safe in Education 2026** was published
**`2026-07-07`** and is in force from **`2026-09-01`**. What changed for this register:

- The **filtering-and-monitoring review** is an at-least-annual duty that must be *properly led,
  evidenced and recorded* — reported as prescribed at **paragraph 171**.
- The DfE's filtering-and-monitoring standards now ask whether systems can handle **"real-time,
  dynamic, personalised and AI-generated content"**, and point schools at the DfE's **Generative AI:
  Product Safety Expectations (January 2026)** and its guidance on applying filtering and monitoring
  rules to AI tools.
- Commentary reports that filtering must **actively block tools capable of creating or altering sexually
  explicit imagery or deepfakes**, treated as a serious form of child-on-child abuse. ⚠️ Secondary
  summary — verify against the statutory text before quoting to a client.
- ⚠️ **Date conflict, recorded not resolved:** one source dates the DfE filtering-and-monitoring standard
  update to **June 2026** alongside revised UK Safer Internet Centre guidance; the others do not mention
  June.

**The prohibition — EU, and there is no grace period.** AI Act **Article 5(1)(f)** bans AI systems that
**infer emotions of natural persons in the workplace and in education institutions**, applicable since
**`2025-02-02`**, with a narrow exception only *"for medical or safety reasons"*. Emotion recognition
outside those two settings is **high-risk** rather than prohibited. The worked examples the commentary
converges on are all education-native: **inferring student attention or interest, affect detection during
an admission test, and affect detection added to online proctoring** — a proctoring tool that flags a
student's stress or nervousness falls inside the ban.

🟢 **The design consequence, stated as the sales argument:** *a compliant EMEA safeguarding build
classifies content and behaviour and never emotional state, and the annual-review evidence pack is the
deliverable.* That is `P251`, and the components are permissive or deployable-as-appliance
(`e2guardian` GPL-2.0, `pi-hole` EUPL, `nsfwjs` MIT, `detoxify` Apache-2.0, `granite-guardian`
Apache-2.0).

⚠️ **Dates this page still does not assert.** The Digital-Omnibus shift of Annex III high-risk education
obligations to **`2027-12-02`** and the **`Regulation (EU) 2026/1744`** citation remain **single-source**
in this base across three passes. Reported, not asserted.

**Non-EU EMEA, from the mandated leg.** The **UAE** Ministry of Education issued **25 generative-AI
prohibitions for schools in February 2026**, covering age suitability, privacy, academic integrity and
exam use — the most prescriptive school-level AI instrument found in the region this pass.

**Adoption context.** An **Epson**-commissioned survey of ~**`3,360`** respondents across the UK, France,
Italy, Germany, Spain and Poland found students driving adoption and **`80%` of teachers worried AI is
entering the classroom faster than schools can manage** — which is, precisely, demand for the governance
layer rather than for more AI. The **DEC Leadership Summit EMEA 2026** convened `41` senior leaders from
`30` institutions across `14` countries in Paris; Eurydice's *Digital education at school in Europe 2026*
and the **OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026** are the two non-vendor baselines to cite.

🔴 **Regional supply note.** The one platform row in this register with EU provenance is a **copyleft
appliance** (`pi-hole`, **EUPL** — a licence whose governing-law clause is EU-specific and which legal
*will* ask about). 🔵 **Say it before they do** (`T432`).

#### 🆕 `p749` (2026-11-10) — the alternative-format layer: two live versions of the harmonised standard, and only one of them confers conformity

🟢 **The finding of the pass for this region, and it is fresh: ETSI, CEN and CENELEC published
EN 301 549 **V4.1.1** on `2026-09-02`** — the first version carrying a compliance framework designed for
the **European Accessibility Act**. 🔴 **But `V3.2.1` remains the version cited in the Official Journal**,
and it is the OJ citation that confers the **presumption of conformity**. ⚠️ **So v4.1.1 is published but
not yet harmonised**, and a conformance claim made against it today may not be worth anything.
**Check the Official Journal on the day** — this is `P249`'s step one, and it is a two-hour task that
protects a whole deliverable.

**The two legal regimes, which clients routinely conflate:**

| Provider | Instrument | Since |
|---|---|---|
| **Public** universities, schools, public bodies | **Web Accessibility Directive** + national transpositions (e.g. Spain's **RD 1112/2018**, which references UNE/EN 301 549 directly) | in force |
| **Private** education providers' digital services | **European Accessibility Act** | **`2025-06-28`** |

🔵 A provost who says "we're covered by the EAA" is usually a public body covered by the WAD, with
different enforcement and a different reporting duty. Getting this wrong mis-scopes the audit.

**Also binding, and in scope for any accessibility product with an AI layer:** EU AI Act **Annex III**
high-risk obligations for education apply from **`2027-12-02`** (consistent with this base's `p745`), with
Article 50 transparency duties already live. 🔴 **And emotion recognition in educational institutions is a
*prohibited* practice** under the Act, in force since February 2025 (`p748`). ⚠️ **An "engagement" or
"attention" detection feature bolted onto an accessibility product is unsellable in EMEA, not merely
regulated** — and vendors do bolt it on, because the same camera pipeline is already there.

**Supply — 🟢 and this is the region where the open-source story is strongest.** The highest-starred
permissive row in the entire tier is **European**:
[`edrlab/thorium-reader`](https://github.com/edrlab/thorium-reader) — **BSD-3-Clause**, `2,937★`, built by
**EDRLab in Paris**, designed for accessibility rather than retrofitted. 🔵 **That provenance is worth
real money in an EMEA procurement**, where "built in Europe, BSD-licensed" answers both the sovereignty
and the licence question at once. Pair it with
[`readium/css`](https://github.com/readium/css) (**BSD-3-Clause**, `127★`) and
[`IBMa/equal-access`](https://github.com/IBMa/equal-access) (**Apache-2.0**, `786★`), whose rule set maps
to **EN 301 549 clauses** rather than only to WCAG success criteria — which is exactly the form an EMEA
audit asks for.

**Adoption context (mandated leg).** Futuresource reports **`67%`** of teachers now using AI tools and
schools moving from isolated pilots to structured implementation with formal policies; an Epson survey
across the UK, France, Italy, Germany, Spain and Poland found teachers worried AI is arriving faster than
schools can manage, with **`76%`** of students expecting to be allowed to use it. The Digital Education
Council's **EMEA summit (Paris)** gathered `41` leaders from `30` institutions across `14` countries and
reported governance and measurement gaps as the leading signal. The Commission's **Eurydice** 2026 report
covers digital/AI integration in school education, and education ministers approved Council conclusions on
teachers in the era of AI in **May 2026**. 🔵 **Governance maturity is the EMEA buying trigger** — and
accessibility conformance is the one governance obligation that is already dated and already enforceable.

#### 🆕 `p740` (2026-11-10) — France has bound what schools may *buy*, and the region's own consortium published the sovereign architecture without a licence

🟢 **The pass's biggest demand finding, and it is a new *kind* of instrument for this base.**
Every EMEA obligation filed here so far regulates **how an institution uses** AI: the AI Act's
Annex III tier at **`2027-12-02`** (stand-alone) and **`2028-08`** (product-embedded) under
**Regulation 2026/1744**, the Digital Omnibus in force July 2026; the transparency and literacy
duties already live; the national designation layer, still stalled in France (the DDADUE bill
passed the Senate in February 2026 and is held in the Assemblée nationale, with DGCCRF listed
provisionally).

🟢 **France's Interoperability Framework for Digital Services for Education, adopted January 2026,
regulates what an institution may buy.** Per 1EdTech's announcement, it requires **public middle
and high schools to use digital tools and services complying with technical requirements for
security, interoperability and responsible digital technology set by the Minister**, and the
framework **favours open standards**. ⚠️ Vendor source; read as secondary and cite it as such.

🔵 **Why that is commercially different from everything else on this page.** An Annex III duty is a
reason to buy **governance**, which is consultative, open-ended and hard to fix-price. A
procurement framework is a reason to buy **conformance**, which is **testable** — and therefore
scopeable, fixed-price-able and acceptance-criteria-able. 1EdTech's own reading is that a vendor
conforming to the framework can **sell into other markets using the same standards**, so the
conformance work amortises across the region. **`P205`'s xAPI conformance spine is the delivery
vehicle and its `MIT` test suite is the acceptance artefact.**

🟡 **The demand context, and it is a counter-signal to `p738`'s `T336`.** The OECD *Digital
Education Outlook 2026* reports **`94 %` of over `23,000` German higher-education students used AI
in 2025, `65 %` daily or weekly** — adoption is settled. But on the same instrument, **teacher
agreement that AI helps with lesson plans runs from `18 %` in France to `91 %` in Viet Nam**.
⚠️ **France is simultaneously the EMEA market with the most binding procurement obligation and the
least convinced teaching workforce.** A proposal whose first slide is *"AI helps teachers"* is
aimed at the `18 %`. A proposal whose first slide is *"this is the conformant, sovereign,
French-hosted way to run it"* is aimed at the obligation — and an obligation does not need
convincing.

🟢 **The supply side answered in the same week, from the region's own institutions.**

#### 🆕 `p738` (2026-11-10) — teachers are past the adoption question, the hard deadline is 2027, and 2026 is the soft-law year to sell into

🟢 **The adoption question is settled in EMEA and a proposal should stop arguing it.**
**Futuresource** reports **`67%` of teachers now using AI tools**, and expects **AI-enabled devices
to reach `15%` of institutional PC shipments in 2026**. An **Epson-commissioned survey of ~`3,360`
respondents across the UK, France, Italy, Germany, Spain and Poland** finds **`76%` of students
expecting to be allowed to use AI in their learning** — and, in the same instrument, **`80%` of
teachers worried that AI is entering the classroom faster than schools can manage.**

🔵 **Those two numbers in one survey are the engagement.** `76%` expectation against `80%` anxiety
is not a technology gap, it is a **capability-and-governance gap**, and it is what the Council of
education ministers formalised in its **conclusions on teachers in the AI era, adopted 11 May 2026**.

🟢 **The regulatory calendar is confirmed again, from a third independent direction, and it matches
what this base published.** A **Digital Omnibus deal reached 7 May 2026** means the **high-risk
rules — which include education — apply from 2 December 2027**, the slip from the original August
2026 date that `T306` closed and `T321` split. Two items are live inside 2026: the Commission's
consultation on **draft high-risk classification guidelines** (open to **23 June 2026**), and the
ministerial conclusions above.

🟡 **So 2026 is a soft-law year with a hard deadline behind it — which is a selling position, not a
lull.** What binds now is AI literacy, transparency and teacher capability (`T321`); what an auditor
reaches for in the absence of applicable regulation is **ISO/IEC 42001**, **UNESCO's generative-AI
guidance** and the **OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026**, all three named in this pass's sources.
🔵 **Quote the OECD's framing in the proposal** — *AI helps learning only when pedagogy stays in
control* — because it justifies the engagement rather than the tool. 🔵 **`Eurydice`'s "Digital
education at school in Europe 2026"** is the comparative instrument for a multi-country bid, and the
**DEC Leadership Summit EMEA 2026** (Paris, `41` senior leaders from `30` institutions across `14`
countries) is the named convening to reference in higher education.

🔴 **One regional correction, because it will recur: the UAE belongs here, not in APAC.** In
**February 2026 the UAE Ministry of Education issued roughly `25` generative-AI prohibitions for
schools** — age suitability, privacy, academic integrity, examination rules. The source that supplied
this filed it as an APAC development. The Gulf is the **M** in EMEA (`T334`). 🔵 **And the substance
inverts the usual assumption**: on this base's reading the Gulf is the **most prescriptive school
regulator of 2026**, more so than any EU member state's national layer — so a Gulf proposal should
lead with compliance, not with speed.

🟢 **Supply here is infrastructure and standards, as it has been for several passes, and this pass
adds three.** [`CrypToolProject/CrypTool-2`](https://github.com/CrypToolProject/CrypTool-2)
(**Apache-2.0**, `169★`, two decades maintained) is the only permissively licensed deployable

(**CC0-1.0**) is the German national metadata profile that makes generated content findable in the

🟡 **And [`hpi-schul-cloud`](https://github.com/hpi-schul-cloud/schulcloud-client) (AGPL-3.0,
`131` repositories, pushed today) is Germany's state school cloud in the open** — unforkable for a

#### 🆕 `p735` (2026-11-10) — 🟢 the Annex III date is RESOLVED (`719-D` closed), and the compliant architecture is now a filable row

🟢 **`719-D` is closed. The EU AI Act Annex III obligations for education bite on `2 December 2027`.**
Six independent legal-practice and regulatory-analysis sources agree on the instrument as well as

| **Two new Article 5 prohibitions** | added by the Omnibus | phase in `2 December 2026` |
| The Annex III obligations themselves | **unchanged in substance** — only the start date moved | `2 December 2027` |

#### 🆕 `p732` (2026-11-10) — the high-risk deadline moved to 2027-12-02; transparency and literacy did not move

**Secondary-source; primary hosts unreachable (`725-F`, `6 / 6` this pass).** The schedule changed
and it changed in the client's favour, which is the single most useful fact in this section.

- 🟢 **The Digital Omnibus on AI — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 — moved the AI Act deadline for
  stand-alone high-risk education systems from `2026-08-02` to `2027-12-02`.** Roughly **16 extra
  months**. ⚠️ Any guidance still citing August 2026 for high-risk education obligations (several
  vendor guides do) **predates the Omnibus and is stale**.
- 🔴 **What did *not* move:** **Article 50 transparency duties apply from `2026-08-02`** — chatbot
  disclosure and synthetic-content marking — i.e. **already in force**. And the **AI-literacy duty
  has applied since `2025-02-02`** to every organisation using AI systems, which includes **every
  school**.
- **High-risk scope in education**: admission decisions, student evaluation and exam scoring.
  Obligations include conformity assessment and **human oversight by qualified staff able to
  monitor, intervene, override and shut the system down**.
- **Enforcement**: the **EU AI Office** (within the Commission) supervises GPAI providers under
  Chapter V; national authorities enforce most else. **Ireland** established the **AI Office of
  Ireland** as an independent statutory body under the *Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Act
  2026*.
- **Council conclusions (2026-10-29)** stress **digital sovereignty and strategic autonomy** and
  reference the **European Digital Education Hub**.

🔵 **Opportunity, and the sequencing is the whole point.** The deadline that binds *now* is
**transparency and literacy**, not high-risk conformity — so the correct EMEA engagement is
**disclosure, synthetic-content marking and staff AI-literacy first**, with high-risk conformity
scoped as a 2027 programme. Selling conformity work as urgent is both wrong and checkable.
🔵 **Exam scoring and admissions are named high-risk**, which makes `P174` the architecture to
propose: a **frozen rubric**, machine-checked state, an auditable mastery record and a human able to
override — the four things a conformity assessment asks for. 🔵 **Sovereignty language in the
Council conclusions keeps the self-hosted, open-weights posture commercially live** in EMEA; pair
with `P175`, which never moves the client's documents off their estate.

⚠️ **Declared supply gap, measured not assumed.** `p732` placed **zero new EMEA rows**. Its
German/French-language legs (`Bildung Lernen KI`, `apprentissage education IA`) returned
`total_count=0` **as composed**; single-term diagnosis shows the pool is real but thin
(`Bildung stars:>5` → `7` repositories in total). The pass's two plausibly-EMEA finds were

**Demand drivers.** Teacher-led adoption running ahead of institutional readiness. Across
six countries, educators adopted AI **autonomously, without a regulatory framework**; in
Spain **>90%** report using AI in their work. Their stated need is **structured training** —
not more tools. Eurydice's *Digital education at school in Europe 2026* reports access to
advanced AI remains uneven across member states.

**Regulation — the most developed in the world, and the main planning input.** The EU AI
Act treats education as **high-risk**. Emotion-recognition AI has been **banned in schools
since February 2025**. High-risk education obligations are reported **delayed to
2 December 2027**, and a Commission Article 6 consultation on draft guidelines ran to
**23 June 2026**. The Council of Europe published a *Compass for AI and Education*; the
Commission updated its AI ethics guidelines for teachers via the European Digital Education Hub.

**Opportunity.** (1) **AI Act conformity work** — high-risk classification means
documentation, risk management and human-oversight design are mandatory, billable, and
deadline-driven ahead of Dec 2027. (2) **Teacher training and enablement**, which is what
the market is actually asking for, mapped to the UNESCO teacher AI competency framework.
(3) Compliance-by-construction reference architectures for EdTech vendors selling into the EU.

generating comparative evidence, and the dates are now specific.** It closes part of this
section's own declared gap (*"no national ministry rollout beyond the UK and UAE"*):

### APAC

#### 🆕 `p768` — 🟢 the **strictest cadence of the four regions**, the only self-reading statutory certificate, and a regulatory picture that is invisible to English queries

🟢 **Japan sets the tightest interval on this register, and it names the school bus explicitly.**

| Instrument | What it sets |
|---|---|
| **道路運送車両法第48条** | 🟢 **a `3`-monthly statutory periodic inspection** for business-use buses — the shortest cadence on any register this base has built |
| **車検** (vehicle inspection) | 🟢 validity of **`1` year** for buses — a second, independent recurrence rule |
| **保安基準第48条の2** | 🟢 a **運行記録計** (tachograph) is required on specified vehicles; extended to the `7`-tonne GVW class from **April 2017**. 🟢 **White-plate (private) buses with capacity `30` or more are included, and school buses are named as a representative example** — this register's exact buyer, in the statute's own illustration |
| Chartered buses (貸切バス) | 🟢 a **digital** tachograph is mandatory, with electromagnetic records retained **`3` years**; analogue switch-off reported **`1 April 2025`** |
| School buses ≥ `11` passengers | 🔵 a `3`-monthly inspection in addition to 車検 is reported, **with the same source noting there is no penalty attached** — treat as unsettled |

🟢 **And the region has the register's best automation case, because the compliance object reads itself.** [`seibii/shaken-qr-reader`](https://github.com/seibii/shaken-qr-reader) (**MIT**, `1,077 B` · `ec1b6f5a6fb9`) decodes the QR code on the **車検証**, so the vehicle register is populated from the statutory certificate with no transcription step (`P348`, `T699`).

🔴 **This entire section exists only because `ACTION p767-A` was executed.** The mandated English and mixed-language leg returned **nothing on Japan at all** — the search result said so explicitly. The Japanese-language leg returned the statutes, the intervals, the retention period and the MIT reader. 🟢 **`運行記録` returns `15` repositories, `車検` returns `100`, `運転日報` `11`, `車検証 QR` `4`**; the English `shaken vehicle inspection japan` returns **`0`** (`T690`).

🔴 **Korea and China are informed gaps on this register.** `자동차검사` returns **`0`** repositories and `운행기록` returns `5`; `车辆年检` returns `26` and `车队管理` `142`, 🔴 **but the Chinese legs are badly polluted — star-ranked results are dominated by `funNLP` (`84,526★`) and the `china-dictatorship` cluster, neither of which is fleet software** (`768-K`). **No Korean or Chinese regulatory instrument was established this pass, and none is claimed.**

**AI-in-education context for the region:** APAC is reported as the **fastest-growing** agentic-AI-in-education market (Mordor) and as holding **`29.0%`** of the broader 2026 market (Coherent). **South Korea's AI Basic Act took effect `22 January 2026`**, described as the region's first comprehensive AI statute; **Vietnam's AI law** followed, with longer transition periods for education, and its high-risk decision **names education and automated assessment** among six sectors; **Vietnam MOET Decision 2422** sets a minimum number of AI content periods per class per year for grades `1`–`12`. **Australia** relies on existing law and voluntary guidance; **Japan** favours voluntary guidelines. **NTU Singapore** gave every undergraduate access to Gemini Enterprise from **August 2026**. Ipsos' 2026 Education Monitor reports support for banning AI in schools **rising in Japan, Australia and South Korea** and **falling in Indonesia**, with Australia and New Zealand highest overall. 🔵 `ACTION p763-D` observed: none of this is filed outside APAC, and no UK or Gulf item has been admitted into this section.

#### 🆕 p765 — the mandate region **and** a genuine supply region, with a dated audit obligation in two Indian jurisdictions

**Register: school-estate safety and statutory compliance.** APAC is the only region this pass found that both mandates school safety audits on a schedule **and** publishes on-register code.

🟢 **India is the clearest mandate on this register anywhere.**

| Instrument | Date | What is owed |
|---|---|---|
| Government Resolution making the Ministry of Education's *Guidelines on School Safety and Security-2021* **mandatory** in one state, building on an earlier resolution of 13 May 2025 | **13 December 2025** | Compliance with the national guidelines |
| Directorate-level circulars | **mid-2026** | Schools must **physically audit themselves** against the *Manual of Safety & Security in School* and **report deficiencies** to the relevant authority |
| Proceedings of the Director of School Education, **Tamil Nadu** | **7 May 2026** | **Every District Chief Education Officer** must complete a school safety and infrastructure audit **in all schools before the June reopening**, benchmarked on the *School Child Safety Handbook 2024-2025*, with each district reporting back to the Directorate |
| **CBSE** affiliation, SARAS portal | **2026-27 session** | The state NOC became **optional**, but a **fire safety certificate from the Fire Services department and a building safety certificate remain mandatory documents** |
| National Building Code of India, Part 4 — Fire and Life Safety | standing | Schools are **Group B (Educational) occupancy** |

🔵 **All of the above is search-sourced from legal and consultancy commentary; no ministry or directorate page was fetched.** One source's claim of a `37 %` first-inspection rejection rate for CBSE affiliation is **not adopted** — no official corroboration was found.

🟢 **APAC supplies code on this register, which is unusual and worth stating plainly.** [`buptlg/fireagent`](https://github.com/buptlg/fireagent) (`77★`, **MIT**, China) is the **highest-starred on-register agent anywhere** — multimodal fire-safety reasoning with evidence grounding, conservative refusal and scene routing that includes `campus`. [`PerryLink/dsh-eia-guide-check`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-eia-guide-check) (**Apache-2.0**) cross-checks environmental-assessment guideline names against current standards — **the closest artefact found anywhere to a statutory-reference validator.** [`AnuwatThisuka/cmms-mcp-server`](https://github.com/AnuwatThisuka/cmms-mcp-server) (**MIT**, Thailand) bridges MES and CMMS work orders. `Safety-Bin/ehs-system` (Korea) compiles statutory review items **and amendment impact** for a site but 🔴 **publishes no grant across `32` paths and `16` manifests.**

🔴 **One APAC artefact is refused on its grant, and the index hid it.** [`arrley/whs-professional-skill`](https://github.com/arrley/whs-professional-skill) (`4★`) is an agent skill for AU/NZ Work Health and Safety professionals whose industry coverage includes education. GitHub's index says `NOASSERTION`; the byte-read grant is **`CC BY-SA 4.0`** (`3,267 B`, `1aa5bca8c8b9`). **ShareAlike on a skill means a derived skill must also be ShareAlike — refused for a proprietary deliverable, and the repository page does not say so** (`T630`, `T646`).

🔴 **`ACTION p763-D` fired again.** The mandated APAC leg returned the **UAE's** February 2026 generative-AI school prohibitions and a **UK** safety standard inside an APAC result set. **Both are EMEA in this base's closed vocabulary. Neither is filed here.** `region` is never populated from a source's own regional framing.

🔴 **Declared gap**: no APAC jurisdiction's statutory interval table was found in code under any licence, and no APAC artefact produces the audit return that India's directorates now require.

#### 🆕 p764 — the largest estate on earth is measured annually to one decimal place, and the two indicators that fail are the two that need design work

**Register: the school estate.** 🟢 **APAC has the best condition telemetry of any region on this register**, and it is published: India's **UDISE+ 2025-26** report, reference year 2025-26, cutoff **`31` March 2026**, covering **`14.67` lakh schools** (`≈1.467` million).

| UDISE+ 2025-26 indicator | Share of schools |
|---|---|
| Drinking water | **`99.5 %`** |
| Any toilet | `99.1 %` |
| Girls' toilets | `98.5 %` |
| Boys' toilets | `97.2 %` |
| Handwashing facility | `96.9 %` |
| Electricity connection | **`95.0 %`** |
| Library | `90.5 %` |
| Computers | `69.9 %` |
| Internet | `67.4 %` (from `63.5 %` in 2024-25) |
| **Ramps with handrails** | 🔴 **`58.2 %`** |
| **CWSN-friendly toilets** | 🔴 **`40.1 %`** |
| Functional rainwater harvesting | 🔴 `29.9 %` |

🟢 **The two failing indicators are the commercially interesting ones.** Water, toilets and electricity are effectively solved at the national level; **accessibility is not** — `40.1 %` for toilets usable by children with special needs, `58.2 %` for ramps with handrails. That is roughly `880,000` schools needing a ramp or an accessible toilet, each requiring a survey, a specification and a works programme.

🔴 **And the indicator is binary.** The report measures whether a facility **exists**, not whether it **functions** — stated in the coverage of the report itself. A `99.5 %` water figure and a broken tap are the same row. 🟢 **Functional-status measurement is the gap, and it is exactly what a condition instrument is for.**

🟢 **The permissive component for the failing indicators already exists and is EMEA-published**: [`sozialhelden/a11yjson`](https://github.com/sozialhelden/a11yjson) (MIT, `1,059 B` · `2b47d728e281`) is a schema for describing the accessibility of physical places, and [`vinnividivicci/ifc-ids-mcp`](https://github.com/vinnividivicci/ifc-ids-mcp) (MIT) turns a written accessibility requirement into an automated check. Neither has ever been pointed at UDISE+.

🔴 **APAC's own supply on this register is a data layer with no grant.** [`datameet/udise_schools`](https://github.com/datameet/udise_schools) (`9★`) and [`gsidhu/udise-district-dump`](https://github.com/gsidhu/udise-district-dump) (`2★`) both returned **no licence payload across `19` paths and `8` manifests** — they are unlicensed scrapes of a national dataset, which is the same shape `p763` recorded for Indonesia's PDDikti. The region's agent-side contributions are real but generic: [`smartaec/ifcMCP`](https://github.com/smartaec/ifcMCP) (Apache-2.0, Tsinghua University, **`17` months stale**), [`General-Soju/BimOnMcp`](https://github.com/General-Soju/BimOnMcp) (MIT) and [`nguyenngocdue/DeepBIM-MCP-Revit-Plugin`](https://github.com/nguyenngocdue/DeepBIM-MCP-Revit-Plugin) (MIT).

🔵 **Regional-framing control, per `ACTION p763-D`**: `p763` recorded that sources return UAE and UK material inside APAC result sets. This block contains **only** instruments of APAC jurisdictions, and every row was placed from the jurisdiction the instrument belongs to, not from the regional framing of the page it was found on.

🟢 **The combined regional play:** build on the permissive APAC model layer, satisfy Korea/Vietnam/TEQSA with the per-institution evidence artefact (`P294`), and keep the input boundary text-only so the same product can be sold into the EU without redesign.

#### 🆕 `p758` — education named as a high-risk sector in a second jurisdiction, and a regulator that now demands a plan per institution

🔴 **Three dated instruments, and two of them are specific to education.**

| Jurisdiction | Instrument | Date | What it obliges |
|---|---|---|---|
| **South Korea** | **AI Basic Act** (Act on the Development of AI and Establishment of Trust) | 🔴 **In force `2026-01-22`** | Transparency, risk assessment, human oversight and documentation for **high-impact** AI systems. ⚠️ Enforcement reported as lenient through 2026 — a guidance-focused grace period rather than penalties |
| **Vietnam** | **Decree 33/2026** | 🔴 **2026** | 🔴 **Names education among six high-risk sectors**, explicitly including **automated assessment** and **behavioural** systems |
| **Australia** | **TEQSA** requirement | 🔴 **2026** | 🔴 **Every higher-education provider must submit an institutional action plan** addressing generative-AI risks |

🔵 **The TEQSA duty is the most directly sellable instrument in any region this pass.** It is not a standard to conform to — it is **a document every provider in the country must produce**, which is a bounded, repeatable engagement with a known buyer and a known artefact. 🟢 **Lead with it in Australia.**

🔴 **Vietnam matters out of proportion to its market size** because it is the second jurisdiction (after the EU) to name education as high-risk *by sector* and to call out automated assessment by name. 🔵 **Read it as confirmation of the direction rather than as a one-country rule**: the assessment layer is where education AI gets regulated first, consistently, across legal traditions.

⚠️ **The regional pattern, as the sources describe it: a patchwork of three approaches** — comprehensive risk-based obligations (South Korea, Vietnam), targeted rules (China), and light-touch models (Japan, Singapore, Australia — with Australia's education-sector duty arriving through its *regulator* rather than through an AI statute). ⚠️ Sources conflict on which framework is furthest along, and none of this could be primary-verified here (`T540`).

🔴 **Extraterritorial exposure is the item APAC vendors most often miss.** The EU AI Act applies to providers and deployers in third countries **where the output is used in the Union**, and Annex III lists education and vocational training as high-risk. 🔵 **An APAC edtech vendor with European users inherits the `2027-12-02` conformity question regardless of its own jurisdiction** — which makes "EU-readiness" a real service line for APAC product companies, not a compliance footnote.

🔴 **The adoption nil, written down.** The mandated leg returned **no classroom-level AI adoption data for any APAC country**. 🔵 This is the second region where the leg returns law rather than measurement, and — per `ACTION p757-D`'s logic, which is now proven on EMEA — **the right response is to stop asking this channel for percentages here too and ask it for duties**, which is what produced the table above. `ACTION p758-G`: re-aim the APAC leg the same way.

🟢 **APAC is the deepest *supply* region in this pass's register, and a client can self-host all of it.** [`k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx`](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) (`Apache-2.0`, `15,870★`, pushed `2026-11-11`), [`wenet-e2e/wenet`](https://github.com/wenet-e2e/wenet) (`Apache-2.0`, `5,255★`), [`OpenMOSS/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize`](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize) (`Apache-2.0`, `2,270★`) and — placed from its own holder line and README — [`AI4Bharat/vistaar`](https://github.com/AI4Bharat/vistaar) (`MIT`, `95★`, India). ⚠️ **Only `vistaar` is regionally placeable from its artifacts**; the other three carry `Apache-2.0` stock text with no holder and no `NOTICE`, so they are recorded **Global** rather than placed from their org names (`T545`).

🔴 **And the code-switching caveat belongs in this region above all others.** Indian and Southeast Asian lecture audio is routinely code-switched, and a headline WER measured on monolingual samples will flatter the pipeline badly. **Measure code-switched audio as its own stratum** (`P289`).

#### 🆕 `p757` (`2026-11-11`) — 🟢 the region supplied the register's **highest-starred** agent and its **only** ethics-paperwork tool; 🔴 and the first of those carries the licence Globant must pass down a contract

🟢 **APAC filed `2` of this pass's `9` agent rows and they are the two extremes of the shelf.** [`SakanaAI/AI-Scientist-v2`](https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist-v2) (Japan) is the register's star attraction at **`7,495★`**, with **`14,979★`** on its byte-identical predecessor. [`htlin222/irb-in-hurry`](https://github.com/htlin222/irb-in-hurry) (Taiwan, `MIT`, `40★`) is the **only artefact on earth this pass found that automates research-ethics paperwork** — `43 / 43` of one cancer centre's official IRB forms from plain text.

🔴 **Read the Sakana licence before the engagement, not after (`T524`).** It is indexed `NOASSERTION`; the payload is a **bespoke** grant titled *The AI Scientist Source Code License v1.0* (December 2025), derived from the **Responsible AI Source Code License v1.1**, byte-read at `4,256 B`, sha256₁₂ `9c82e554a54d`. **It is not OSI-approved and it is not non-commercial** — commercial use *is* granted. What it carries instead:

| Clause | Obligation | Why it reaches Globant |
|---|---|---|
| `3.2(e)` — the *"AI Scientist"* clause | Manuscripts, research papers or technical reports it generates must **prominently disclaim** machine generation (abstract, Disclosure or Methods) | The deliverable's **content** is constrained, not just its attribution |
| `3.2(a)`–`3.2(d)` | No surveillance / protected-class inference, no undisclosed synthetic media, no unsupervised diagnosis, no criminality prediction | Standard RAIL-family behavioural restrictions |
| 🔴 `3.3` | Those restrictions **MUST be included as an enforceable provision in any legal agreement** governing Your use or distribution | 🔴 **A contract-drafting obligation on the integrator.** The restrictions must appear in **Globant's own client agreement** |
| `4` | Breach of `3.2` lets the Licensor **terminate and require destruction of all copies** | A live termination risk carried into a client deployment |

🔵 **The commercial read:** this is the agent every research client will have seen, and it is usable — but it is the **only** row in this pass that changes what Legal has to draft. Price the clause, or pick [`microsoft/RD-Agent`](https://github.com/microsoft/RD-Agent) (`MIT`, `15,322★`), which is permissive and does the same class of work without the flow-down. ⚠️ Sakana's last push is **`2025-12-19`** — roughly eleven months cold.

🟢 **The provenance standard is half-APAC and that is a credible regional claim.** [`ResearchObject/ro-crate`](https://github.com/ResearchObject/ro-crate)'s copyright is held jointly by the **University of Technology Sydney** and the University of Manchester — the packaging standard for "what an agent produced and how" is co-owned in this region.

🔴 **The gap, measured and regional.** There is **no open-source research-administration platform anywhere in APAC** that this pass could find: no grants system, no ethics-review workflow, no CRIS. The entire regional supply for the register is one bespoke-licensed research agent and one MIT form generator. 🔵 **Against that, the region's AI governance is the most dated in the world** — Korea's **AI Basic Act in force `2026-01-22`**, **Vietnam's AI law in force `2026-03-01`** with **transition periods of 12 months, or 18 months in health care, education and finance**, China regulating through targeted measures including content labelling, while **Australia and Japan rely on existing law plus voluntary guidance** and **Singapore on frameworks such as AI Verify**. ⚠️ Those are regional AI statutes, **not research-administration rules**, and are recorded as the governance context a research-integrity deliverable is sold into — not as a mandate for it.

#### 🆕 `p756` (`2026-11-11`) — 🟢 compulsory AI curriculum lands in **2026–27** in both giants, and national curriculum structure for Korea and China is now held permissively

🟢 **The mandate is now dated in both of the region's largest systems.** China's **Ministry of Education** formalised **"Artificial Intelligence and Technology"** as a school subject for the **2026–27** year — read by at least one analysis as industrial policy rather than curriculum reform. **India** brings AI and computational thinking into all schools **from Grade 3** starting **2026–27**, tied to **NEP 2020**. 🔵 Both join the mandatory-AI-literacy group with the UAE. **Vietnam** classes education as a high-risk sector and names **automated assessment** and behavioural monitoring (`p745`'s `Decision No. 33/2026/QD-TTg`, search-channel only). Binding regimes: **South Korea, China and Vietnam**; Japan, Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia and India rely mainly on existing law and guidance, and India's amended IT Rules on **labelling synthetic content** took effect **`2026-02-20`**.

🟢 **Scale and sentiment.** China's State Council **"AI Plus"** target is a **`90%`** penetration rate for new-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents **by 2030**, `70%` by 2027; CNNIC counts **`700`+ million** generative-AI users by mid-2026. 🔵 **Public opinion is the region's quiet advantage:** the **Ipsos Education Monitor 2026** puts support for *banning* AI in schools at **`26%` in India**, with Australia and New Zealand materially higher. **Permission to deploy is highest where the mandates are.**

🟢 **The supply gap this pass closes is the right asset for a curriculum mandate.** A compulsory subject creates immediate demand for **curriculum-aligned sequencing**, and this pass recovered national curriculum structure for both giants, permissively: [`DECK6/korean-elementary-learning-map`](https://github.com/DECK6/korean-elementary-learning-map) (**MIT**, `1,544 B`, sha256₁₂ `5464fb2fa5ef`) and [`wwlwgo/cn-primary-math-knowledge-graph`](https://github.com/wwlwgo/cn-primary-math-knowledge-graph) (**MIT**, `1,118 B`, `d20c5af7d2b5`). 🔵 **Why structure beats a model here:** knowledge tracing needs a *skill* taxonomy to trace against, or it traces item IDs and cannot explain a recommendation to a teacher — and a ministry introducing a subject will ask for exactly that explanation (`P282`).

🔴 **Two APAC-placed recoveries are restricted and are filed as warnings.** [`heronerar/OpenGaokao`](https://github.com/heronerar/OpenGaokao) carries a bespoke **"OpenGaokao Source-Available License 1.0"** stating in its own text that it is **not an OSI-recognised open-source licence** and restricting commercial use (`15,992 B`, `94ca1c665a33`); [`michael-borck/assessment-rubrics-for-ai`](https://github.com/michael-borck/assessment-rubrics-for-ai) (Curtin University, Australia) reserves all materials as the author's intellectual property with use permitted inside Curtin. 🔵 **Both would have read as plausible picks from their names alone.**

#### 🆕 `p755` (`2026-11-11`) — 🟢 the world's largest adult-literacy programme: `40.3` million learners, **zero AI**, on a stack this base already holds as permissive

🟢 **This is the largest single opportunity in the register, and for once the APAC leg breaks a nil from the policy side rather than the repository side.** India's **ULLAS / New India Literacy Programme**, on the record: a centrally sponsored scheme with an outlay of **₹`1,037.90` crore for FY `2022-23` to FY `2026-27`**, targeting **all non-literates aged `15` years and above**; **~`4.03` crore (`40.3` million) registered learners**; **ten States/UTs declared fully literate between `2024` and `2026`**, with **Uttarakhand the sixth in July `2026`**. Delivery is explicitly multi-channel and low-bandwidth — the scheme's own materials state that *"all material and resources shall be provided digitally through TV, radio, and phone-based apps and portals"*, while volunteer training stays face-to-face — via the **DIKSHA + ULLAS app in `22` Indian languages**. The app also handles **learner and volunteer registration during door-to-door surveys** and programme monitoring. Assessment is the **FLNAT**, run **twice every year**, covering reading, writing, numeracy **and digital and financial literacy**.

🔴 **No AI component was found anywhere in the scheme's own materials.** 🟢 **And DIKSHA runs on Sunbird, which this base already holds as MIT and cites `533` times** — so the integration target is on these shelves, the data model exists, and the volunteer and survey records are already there (`P276`). 🔴 **The clock is explicit and short: the outlay ends FY `2026-27` and no successor programme was found.** 🔵 **Read that as the procurement window rather than as a risk** — a successor scheme is precisely where an AI layer gets specified, and specifying it is the engagement.

🟢 **The regional policy frame is converging on lifelong learning from outside the region too.** The **OECD's `Skills in the AI age`** paper (`2026`) recommends expanding lifelong learning by promoting continuous upskilling and reskilling and broadening access to AI learning beyond specialists; the **ILO** (May `2026`) urges governments to elevate lifelong learning to a central pillar of economic and social policy, warning that without inclusive learning systems the transformations **risk widening inequalities**. 🔵 Both are leverage for a ministry conversation; neither is an APAC instrument.

🔴 **Declared gaps, stated explicitly rather than left silent.** **No APAC adult-education repository row this pass, and the candidate was tested rather than assumed:** [`qwertyuiop9898123/KouninPass`](https://github.com/qwertyuiop9898123/KouninPass) (`0★`) is Japanese *kōsotsu-nintei* high-school-equivalency prep **with past exam PDFs and automated grading** — functionally on-register and the only APAC candidate found — and it carries **no grant at any of ten probed addresses**, so it is published **unplaced-as-licensed** and the APAC repository nil holds (`T492`). 🔴 **No APAC AI-in-adult-education regulation found**: the first regional search returned nothing on India, China or Japan policy at all, and the ULLAS material contains no AI provision. 🔴 **The ULLAS figures above are search-channel-sourced only** — government hosts are unreachable in this session (`T502`) — **and two sources disagree on the fully-literate state count, so the `10` States/UTs figure is reported with its provenance and not as a settled number.**

#### 🆕 `p754` (`2026-11-10`) — 🟢 the only region where the **state** ships early-childhood AI at scale, and the permissive substrate is already deployed there

🟢 **China — the only national AI-in-education plan found this pass that names the early years.** The **Ministry of Education with four other departments launched an "AI + Education" action plan in April `2026`, spanning early childhood through lifelong learning.** Scale: **~`36M` children across `250,000`+ kindergartens**. The research is operational rather than aspirational — a `2026` study tests **LLMs as assessment teammates for teacher–child interaction quality** in Chinese preschools, framing AI as the only route to quality monitoring at that scale; a March `2026` study of `50` Froebelian practitioners found a **"dual-track"** practice combining hands-on nature-based play with AI personalisation, with explicit concern about displacing sensory experience. 🔴 **Supply caution: the highest-starred preschool application on GitHub is Chinese — [`yuxink/joye-preschool`](https://github.com/yuxink/joye-preschool) (`39★`, 幼小衔接 school-readiness) — and it carries no grant at `8` probed paths. Globant may not build on it.**

🟢 **India — the register's clearest state-scale opportunity, and the substrate is already in place.** Public pre-primary runs through **~`1.37M` anganwadi centres** under ICDS, with nutrition tracked via **Poshan Tracker**; the **first "AI-powered anganwadi"** (Waddhamna, near Nagpur) uses VR, smartboards and tablets, with plans to scale to `40` more centres and AI-based nutrition tracking. 🟢 **The permissive platform family behind that digitisation is on this base's shelf: [`dimagi/commcare-hq`](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-hq) (`525★`, **`BSD-3-Clause`**, pushed the day of this pass) — fork, extend, rebrand and bill** (`P272`). 🔴 **The curriculum policy, however, excludes the early years: AI and computational thinking enter from Class `3` in the `2026`–`27` session, while the `3`–`6` band is not addressed** — a stated gap rather than an opportunity closed (`T486`).

🟢 **Australia — the register's only real agent.** [`MengC-OvO/easy-teaching`](https://github.com/MengC-OvO/easy-teaching) (`58★`, **MIT**, `f755cdc76e68`, pushed `2026-09-16`) is a **safety-aware teacher agent for Australian early-childhood education**, and simultaneously one of only **two** repositories the `early childhood education stars:>20` query returns at all. 🔵 **"Safety-aware" is the finding: in ECEC the duty-of-care constraints are the product** (`T487`).

🟢 **Indonesia** contributes the localisation shell [`khorihutama/tumbuh-kembang`](https://github.com/khorihutama/tumbuh-kembang) — 🟡 **MIT code with its Denver II–derived dataset expressly carved out of the grant** (`T485`). 🔵 **Reading: APAC is where this register's demand is named, funded and state-scale, and where `3` of the pass's `6` agent rows originate.**

#### 🆕 `p753` (`2026-11-10`) — 🔴 the largest supply on earth and two-thirds of it carries no licence: the clearance phase *is* the opportunity

🔴 **APAC has the biggest regional head in this register and the worst licence hygiene measured by this base in any register.** `indian sign language` → **`2,732`** repositories. Licence distribution of the top `50` by stars: **`33` `NONE` (`66%`)**, `7` MIT, `4` Apache-2.0, `4` GPL-3.0, `2` GPL/LGPL-2.x. Byte-read control on the three highest-starred `NONE` rows: `3 / 3` genuinely have **no grant** (`EvilPort2/Sign-Language` `824★`, `satyam9090/…` `140★`, `shag527/…` `127★`) (`T472`).

🟢 **So the APAC engagement is shaped differently from every other region's:** it opens with a **licence-clearance and data-provenance phase** — now scopeable with a number, `66%` — then trains on **client-owned, consented** signing data, using the Apache-2.0 AI4Bharat architecture as the reference and expecting to carry its maintenance. Recipe `P269`.

🟢 **Policy context read this pass:** **UAE Ministry of Education `25` generative-AI prohibitions for schools (February 2026)** — age suitability, privacy, academic integrity, exam restrictions — the most prescriptive school-level GenAI instrument any pass of this base has read; **UK DfE generative-AI safety standards (January 2026)**; World Bank **Global EdTech Policy Academy, Seoul, `2026-08-31`–`09-04`**; Ipsos Education Monitor 2026 finds *lower* support for school AI bans across the Asian markets surveyed. 🟢 **A region that prohibits specific uses rather than deferring the whole programme is a region where a narrowly-scoped accessibility deliverable passes review.**

#### 🆕 `p752` (`2026-11-10`) — 🔴 an informed nil on native supply, a named route in, and the sharpest education-specific high-risk rule in any region

🔴 **The nil, measured and written down rather than left blank:** `asean skills framework open source` → **`0`** repositories. `india nco occupation classification` → **`4`** (all hobby-scale). 🔴 **There is no native open-source occupational-taxonomy or skills-extraction stack for this region.** That is a measurement, not an omission.

🟢 **The route in, and it is the only one found.** Tabiya's publisher names **South Asia** among its partner regions, and [`tabiya-tech/taxonomy-model-application`](https://github.com/tabiya-tech/taxonomy-model-application) (**MIT**, `20★`, pushed `2026-11-10`) is built specifically to **derive a localised national taxonomy** from an ESCO-derived reference model — which is exactly the need in a country that has no maintained national classification, or has one that no API serves. 🟢 **`P263` on [`../compose/patterns.md`](../compose/patterns.md) is the engagement pattern**: localisation of a permissive platform, **not** adoption of a local stack, because no local stack exists (`T462`). 🟡 At `14★`–`20★` Globant adopts the architecture and carries the maintenance — say so in the proposal.

🔴 **The regulatory picture is the most consequential for this register of any region, because one country names education AI as high-risk in sector-specific terms:**

| Jurisdiction | Instrument | What it means for a skills or assessment agent |
|---|---|---|
| 🇻🇳 **Vietnam** | A **July 2026** decision identifies high-risk AI systems across **six sectors, including education** — naming automated assessment and behavioural tools | 🔴 **The most education-specific high-risk designation found in any region.** Note the qualifier: many listed systems count as high-risk **only when their output is used in certain ways**, so *how* a Globant deliverable's output is consumed is part of the compliance analysis, not just what it computes. |
| 🇰🇷 **Korea** | **AI Basic Act**, in force **`2026-01-22`**; enforcement decrees still being finalised | 🟡 Grace period through 2026 focused on guidance rather than penalties — a window, and it is closing. |
| 🇨🇳 **China** | Mandatory registration, strict content-labelling obligations | 🔴 Penalties to **¥50M**. The most developed framework in the region. |
| 🇦🇺 **Australia** | **TEQSA** requires **all** higher-education providers to file institutional action plans addressing generative-AI risk | 🟢 **A named, universal, institution-level deliverable — this is a concrete services opportunity, not just a constraint.** |
| 🇯🇵 **Japan** | Principles-based; cooperation and existing law rather than penalties | 🟡 Transparency expectations still apply. |
| 🇸🇬 **Singapore** | **AI Verify** toolkits rather than hard law | 🟢 Testing-and-attestation route; useful as an assurance artefact. |

🔴 **Cross-border exposure is real and often missed in APAC scoping:** the EU AI Act's education and recruitment high-risk categories **reach APAC providers serving EU learners or employers**, on the `2026-12-02`… **`2 December 2027`** Annex III timeline. 🔵 *Sources conflict on several of these dates; verify against final texts before quoting to a client.*

🔵 **Opportunity, placed.** 🟢 **The two buyable engagements here are different in kind:** (a) **taxonomy localisation** via `P263` for ministries and development programmes in South and Southeast Asia, where supply is nil; and (b) **AI governance and assurance work** — Australia's TEQSA action plans, Singapore's AI Verify attestations, Korea's pre-decree readiness — which is advisory-plus-implementation work that the measured absence of local open-source supply does nothing to diminish. 🔴 **Do not propose a single APAC approach: the regulatory instruments differ by country more sharply here than in any other region.**


#### 🆕 `p751` — the scheduling and assignment register, placed in APAC

🔴 **APAC has the binding pre-launch control that no other region has, and it lands on exactly this register.** China's framework — covering algorithmic recommendation, deep synthesis and generative AI — requires public-facing services to complete a **security assessment and algorithm filing *before* launch**. 🔴 **A public-facing school-place allocation or timetable-publication service in China is therefore a filing exercise before it is an engineering exercise**, and that sequencing has to be in the plan from day one rather than discovered at go-live.

🟢 **Curriculum demand is the strongest in the world here.** **China and the UAE are the only countries with compulsory national AI curricula**, starting in the 2025-26 school year, and China's Ministry of Education has published K-12 AI-literacy curriculum guidelines. **India** plans AI and computational thinking compulsory **from Class 3**, tied to the IndiaAI Mission with a large teacher-training push, placed in the **2026-27 academic year**. 🔵 Compulsory curriculum at national scale is a timetabling problem before it is a pedagogy problem — every mandated subject has to be fitted into a fixed week, and that is this register's core product.

🔴 **Vietnam is the APAC jurisdiction that names this register's risk directly.** A **July 2026 decision identifies high-risk AI systems in six sectors, including education**, with coverage read as extending to **automated assessment**. **India's** statutory position is contested in the sources read this pass — one July 2026 source says the government signalled it may pursue dedicated AI legislation, another says no comprehensive law is close; the **February 2026 amendments to the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 took effect `2026-02-20`** and target AI-generated content rather than allocation decisions. 🔵 **This base records the disagreement rather than resolving it.**

🔴 **The APAC open-source supply for this register is a measured nil, and it is a real finding rather than a thin search.** `india school timetable open source` returns **`0` repositories**. The one APAC-placed portal agent found, [`techkwon/comci-agent`](https://github.com/techkwon/comci-agent) (Comci, 🇰🇷 Korea, `1★`), is indexed **`NOASSERTION`** and was **not shelved** — there is no grant to rely on. 🟢 **Opportunity:** the largest school systems on earth are adopting compulsory AI curricula into fixed timetables with **no permissive regional scheduling stack at all**; the substrate (`or-tools`, `timefold-solver`) is permissive and jurisdiction-neutral, and the localisation — calendars, shift patterns, exam boards, language — is the billable layer.

#### 🆕 `p750` (2026-11-10) — the wellbeing and safeguarding layer: the region is moving to restriction rather than governance, and the one MIT artefact in the register was publicly funded here

🟢 **The region's live story is Australia, and it broke the day before this pass.** On **`2026-11-09`**
the ABC reported the federal government moving to reduce classroom screen time via a new **"digital
detox" taskforce**, with generative AI to be **restricted in primary schools and in high-school
assessment**. 🔵 **Read the direction, not just the policy:** APAC's leading system is answering the
wellbeing question with *less* technology in the classroom, which reframes a studio's pitch from
"deploy AI" to "govern and evidence what is already there".

**The safeguarding incidents are AI-native and already counted.** eSafety warned in **July 2026** about
AI misuse of school photography, after **more than `100` reports in early 2026** of anonymous accounts
targeting schools and staff with **AI-manipulated content harvested from school social media**, advising
a risk-based approach to posting student images plus an incident-response plan. 🔴 **This is the same
demand KCSIE 2026 creates in the UK, arriving through a regulator's advisory instead of statutory
guidance.**

**Exposure is measured.** eSafety reported in **March 2026** that **`79%` of children aged 10–17 had used
an AI assistant or AI companion**. 🔵 **That figure is the whole business case for the wellbeing register
in this region:** the companion relationship is already normal, and nobody is governing it.

**The governance instrument is voluntary.** The Australian Framework for Generative AI in Schools is
**guidance, not law** — `6` principles supported by **`25` guiding statements**, with **no enforcement
mechanism**; its wellbeing principle requires that tools not compromise student mental health. On data,
**`7` of the `8`** government school systems limit or advise against identifiable student information in
AI tools, and **Western Australia has no public departmental AI policy**. 🟢 **A voluntary framework plus
a per-jurisdiction data rule is exactly the shape that sells an assurance and evidence engagement.**

🟢 **The supply-side find, and it belongs to this region.** The one **MIT**-licensed intervention engine
in the whole register — [`abelardopardo/ontask_b`](https://github.com/abelardopardo/ontask_b) (`45★`) —
carries the payload line *"Copyright (c) 2017 **Office for Learning and Teaching. Australian
Government**"*. 🔵 **Publicly funded in APAC, permissively licensed, and effectively unknown**: lead with
it in a regional proposal (`P254`). ⚠️ Last push `2025-04-10`.

**India — the mandate exists and the evaluation does not.** **CBSE** affiliation bye-laws require each
affiliated secondary and senior-secondary school to appoint a **Counsellor and Wellness Teacher**;
Navodaya Vidyalayas provide for **two contractual counsellors** per school. The Ministry of Education's
**Manodarpan** programme runs a national helpline plus *Sahyog* sessions and *Paricharcha* webinars, and
had taken **`332,877` helpline calls by `2026-03-10`**. 🔴 **A 2026 analysis states no single summative
impact evaluation has been conducted and flags sustainability risk from reliance on voluntary
counsellors.** 🟢 **That gap — a national programme at scale with no measurement layer — is a
ministry-tier opportunity, and `getodk/central` + `commcare-hq` are the permissive instruments for it.**
⚠️ A blog claim that a national School Mental Health Policy was due **`2026-06-01`** could not be
confirmed against an official source.

**Regional attitude.** The **Ipsos Education Monitor 2026** finds **weaker support for banning AI in
schools** across the Asian markets surveyed, even while support for restricting children's social media
stays high. 🔵 **So the APAC buyer wants AI with guardrails, not AI removed** — which is in direct
tension with the Australian direction above, and the tension is the thing to name in a regional pitch.

🔴 **Informed gap — the leg ran and returned nothing.** The targeted leg for **Japan and South Korea**
school suicide-prevention and AI-based risk screening **returned no usable facts**. Korea's AI Basic Act
(in force `2026-01-22`, education treated as high-impact) is held elsewhere on this page; **the
wellbeing-specific instruments for both countries remain unmeasured by this base.** Recorded as a gap so
silence is not read as coverage.

#### 🆕 `p749` (2026-11-10) — the alternative-format layer: the standard is being revised upward, the regulator is not yet conformant itself, and private institutions are now on the hook

🔴 **Japan is the region's live story, and it has three distinct moving parts.**

1. **The standard is being revised toward WCAG 2.2** — `JIS X 8341-3`, reported `2026-10-19` as its first substantive revision in roughly a decade. ⚠️ **Sources conflict on the target**: one account says the revision aims at **WCAG 2.1 AA** with government sites expected to comply by **end-2026**, another says it targets **WCAG 2.2**. 🔵 **Recorded as a conflict rather than resolved**, because the difference changes a client's test plan materially. The Digital Agency's own policy page currently names **`JIS X 8341-3:2016` and WCAG 2.2**, at **Level AA**.
2. 🔴 **The regulator is not yet conformant itself.** The Digital Agency's FY2025 accessibility review, published **`2026-03-31`**, reported only **partial Level A** compliance on its own pages. 🔵 **This is a useful and disarming fact in a Japanese engagement:** the benchmark is aspirational across the board, so a credible staged remediation plan beats a promise of full conformance.
3. 🟢 **Private institutions are now in scope.** The **2024 amendment** to Japan's disability discrimination act made **reasonable accommodation mandatory for private bodies** — which reaches private schools, universities and *juku*. ⚠️ Several sources still describe private-sector web compliance as voluntary; **those two statements are about different duties** and the accommodation duty is the one that bites.

**The rest of the region, with its gaps stated.** 🟡 **Australia**: federal government sites are required to
meet **WCAG 2.1 AA** under the Digital Service Standard — **not confirmed against a primary government
source this pass**, and the Disability Discrimination Act is the underlying instrument. 🟡 **India**:
**IS 17802** is the national ICT accessibility standard, aligned to WCAG and updated in 2023, with the
**RPWD Act** framework described as enforceable — 🔴 **nothing found on how either reaches universities**.
🔴 **No APAC country was found this pass with an education-specific digital accessibility deadline of the
kind North America and EMEA now have.** ⚠️ **That is an informed gap, not coverage:** the duties exist, but
they arrive through disability-discrimination law and procurement standards rather than through a dated
education rule, so the commercial trigger is weaker and the sales motion is different.

**Supply — nothing in this tier is APAC-published.** 🔴 All `18` rows filed this pass originate in North
America or Europe (DAISY Consortium, W3C, EDRLab, Readium, IBM, Microsoft, Google, ASU, APH, NV Access).
🔵 **The language consequence is the opportunity.** `liblouis` carries braille tables for many languages
and is **LGPL-2.1**, so it can be extended; but the *speech* layer is thin for the region's languages, and
`espeak-ng` (**GPL-3.0**, `7,022★`) is the only broad open voice set — copyleft, so `P248`'s boundary
applies. 🟢 **CJK and Indic alternative-format production is the clearest unclaimed niche in this whole
register**, and the permissive checker layer (`daisy/ace`, `epubcheck`, `MathCAT`) works regardless of
script.

**Adoption context (mandated leg).** Times Higher Education (April 2026) describes **uneven** uptake of
advanced AI across the region with connectivity a likely constraint, and virtual tutors used by **`30%`**
of a surveyed cohort; Ipsos's Education Monitor 2026 found **weaker** public support for banning AI in
Asian schools than for restricting children's social media. The **UAE Ministry of Education** reportedly
introduced **`25`** generative-AI prohibitions for schools in **February 2026** (secondary source — verify
against the ministry's own publication). EdTech Hub launched AI-in-education briefs for **Southeast Asia**
in March 2026, explicitly covering **marginalised learners** — 🟢 the closest thing in the region to an
accessibility-adjacent policy hook, and worth tracking.


#### 🆕 `p748` (2026-11-10) — the money layer: the region with real national entitlement code, and the only region where both new agent rows were built in-market

**Demand — 🟢 fast adoption, fragmented governance, and that combination is the sale.** Growth is
the strongest of any region (MarketsandMarkets puts the regional AI-in-education CAGR at **`20.9%`**
for 2024-29, while North America still holds revenue share); an EdTech Hub figure reports roughly
**`86%` of Southeast Asian teachers already using AI tools**, and **fewer than half** of surveyed

Philippines' DepEd working through **SEAMEO INNOTECH** and launching **AGAP.AI** in January 2026 as
its first nationwide responsible-AI programme in basic education. **Clarivate** published a
comparative study of AI policy across **seven** Asia-Pacific jurisdictions; Cambridge English
convened **200+** senior leaders including ministries. ⚠️ **Gap recorded honestly: the mandated leg
surfaced no primary regulatory text for China, Japan, Korea, Australia or India** — the picture is
Southeast-Asia-weighted and partly vendor-sourced.

both of this pass's in-market agent rows.**
